transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, honestly, what made me come in is that I keep getting up during our long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to just stay seated, but... I don't know, I just end up getting out of my chair anyway, even if it’s just to go refill my water or pace by the printer for a bit.
Did you have similar difficulties staying seated or feeling restless back when you were a child in school?

Yeah, actually. I remember this starting way before high school. Um, my elementary school teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I rushed through things. I talked out of turn a lot, forgot my homework... and my desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. So, yeah, it's been going on for a while.

Sorry, do I currently... what? I think you might have trailed off there. 

But if you mean things like the forgetfulness or the messy desk from when I was younger, um... I haven't really noticed that being a problem for me lately. I manage my sales accounts pretty well and keep on top of my emails. It's really just the restlessness and having to get up during those long meetings that stands out to me right now. Was there something specific you were wondering about?
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by unrelated thoughts or things going on around you?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I get distracted that easily. If I'm working on a client pitch or something, I can usually tune out what's going on around the office. My mind doesn't really wander off to unrelated things. Like I said, it's really just my body wanting to get up and move, rather than my focus drifting.
